feature: Layer names on the timing strip wrap instead of being cut
summary: A layer name too long for one line of the timing strip now takes a second line beside its kind mark, the way the Make a bell swing mock wraps Bell body, so names like Notification bell and Settings window read whole without pointing at them. Every heading is drawn bright, as the mock draws them.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: timing-strip-long-names-walk (no flags).

try.do: Open any picture, draw a rectangle and name it Notification bell (double-click its row in Layers).
Pick Rotation from Add Motion in the Motion section, so the strip opens across the bottom.
Draw an ellipse called Settings window and a rectangle called Title text layer, and give each a Rotation.
Read the strip's headings: each long name sits whole on two lines beside its mark, and the bars still start at 0 on the ruler.
Name a fourth layer settings-capture-top-left-corner-shadow and give it a Rotation: only this one is cut in the middle.
Rest the pointer on that cut heading to read it whole on the tooltip.
Compare with the mock's timing dock, mock on top and the app below.

evaluate: Do Notification bell, Settings window and Title text layer read at a glance on two lines?
Is a taller row for a two-line name a fair price, or does a strip of long names now feel too tall?
With every heading bright, can you still tell which layer is picked from its bars' blue ring alone?
Is cutting only names that two lines cannot hold the right line to draw?
rough: The name column stays 92 points where the mock's is 58 pixels, so the app wraps later than the mock: Bell body fits on one line here. Narrowing it would move where the bars start, so it is your call on card the-timing-strip-s-name-column-is-as-wide-as-the-how-wide-should-the-column-of-la.
A two-line heading makes its row about 10 points taller. The strip now grows to 220 points before it scrolls (was 188), so four layers with two-line names still show without scrolling.
Every heading is now drawn bright, as the mock draws them; before, headings of layers not picked were dimmed. The picked layer is shown by the blue ring on its bars.
